title: Forces and Newton's Laws
seo_title: Physics 1: Forces and Newton's Laws Worksheets (Strengthened SHS)
standard_text: Types of forces; Newton's laws of motion; free-body diagrams; weight, normal force and friction; applications of Newton's laws. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Physics 1, Quarter 2)
meta_desc: Free Physics 1 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 2): newton's laws of motion, resultant force and free-body diagrams, mass, weight and gravity, friction and forces in action. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Fnet = ma: the resultant force decides the acceleration.
body_html:
How to think about it

Newton's first law: an object keeps its velocity unless a resultant force acts. Second law: Fnet = ma. Third law: forces come in pairs that are equal in size, opposite in direction and act on different objects.

Draw a free-body diagram, add the forces as vectors and use Fnet = ma. Weight Fg = mg with g = 9.8 N/kg on Earth. Friction opposes sliding: Ff = μFN, with static friction usually larger than kinetic friction.

Example

A 1,200 kg car accelerates at 2.5 m/s². Resultant force?

F = ma = 1,200 × 2.5

Answer: 3,000 N

Example

A 20 kg box on a horizontal floor, μk = 0.30. Kinetic friction?

FN = 20 × 9.8 = 196 N

Ff = 0.30 × 196

Answer: 58.8 N

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a moving object needs a resultant force to keep moving at constant speed.
  • Putting both forces of an action–reaction pair on the same object.
  • Confusing mass (kg) with weight (N).

faq.q: Why do you lurch forward when a bus brakes?
faq.a: Your body keeps moving forward (inertia) while the bus slows down.

faq.q: Is the normal force always equal to the weight?
faq.a: Only on flat, horizontal ground with no other vertical forces; on a ramp or in an accelerating elevator it is different.

items.q: Pushing an empty cart makes it speed up more than pushing a full one. Which law does this best show?

items.e: Acceleration depends on resultant force and mass.

items.q: Why do passengers fall forward when a bus stops suddenly?

items.q: Action and reaction forces act on…

items.e: So they never cancel each other.
